access.edition_or_version: Macmillan, London, 1917 English edition, trans. Surendranath Tagore under the author's supervision (public domain in the US); Bengali original listed 1911 (works-list record, 2026-09-24).

tone_mechanisms_observed: looking-back lexis framing recollection as interpretation rather than reliving
periodic sentences that subordinate the remembered incident to the interpreting clause — the reflection grammatically governs the memory
narrated past with reflective present detaching at interpretive cruxes: past event, present understanding
reflection remains outward-turned — toward people, music, landscape — resisting the navel-gazing failure by keeping the object of attention outside the self
mechanics.point_of_view: Retrospective adult self observing the child-self as a figure: two distinct selves in one utterance, the memoir-specific form of self-distancing.
mechanics.tense_and_structure: Predominant narrated past of the reminiscence with reflective present at interpretive cruxes; episodic accretion over years.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Unhurried accretion of episodes; reflective pauses fall at scene boundaries, so reflection never blocks incident flow (supports clm-tone-reflective-causal-momentum).
mechanics.psychic_distance: The composing adult-self stands at chronological distance from the experiencing child-self — retrospective step-back built into the memoir form.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Concrete persons and places carry the reflection; memory figures of light and awakening used sparingly (paraphrased — no wording reproduced).
mechanics.copyright_note: 1917 English edition public domain in the US (pre-1929); Bengali original public domain. Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
mechanics.translation_note: The reflective-evaluative cadence observed in English is partly the translator's; Bengali rhythmic and idiomatic texture is not carried — see src-reflective-tagore-reminiscences-1917.
